name: hgraph
description: The dependency graph — Horizon's vendored hgraph core keeps one file per statement/Lean declaration under <project>/hgraph/; `horizon graph frontier` ranks work and agents attach node-scoped comments and reviews. This is the only DAG engine.
---

Each project may carry an **hgraph**: a plain-files semantic graph under
`<project>/hgraph/` — one Markdown node per blueprint statement and per Lean
declaration, typed edges (`uses` = the hard dependency DAG, `formalizes` =
informal↔formal identity). `horizon graph sync` (run automatically at run boundaries)
reconciles the blueprint + Lean sources into it; your **authored** additions
(comments, reviews, metadata) are never touched by sync. The files are
committed to the workspace ledger like everything else.

Use `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …`; when a workspace has one project,
`-p` is optional. Address nodes by `label:<latex-label>` or
`decl:<lean-fqname>` — raw ids are opaque hashes. Most commands accept `--json`.

## Sync it yourself — and act on the warnings

Don't wait for the run boundary: after you change blueprint statements,
`\uses{}`/`\lean{}` annotations, or Lean declarations, run
`"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> sync` and **read its output**. Sync prints warnings for exactly the defects
you can fix on the spot: `\uses{X} has no blueprint node` (missing/mistyped
label), `\lean{Name} not found in Lean sources` (renamed or unwritten
declaration), stale nodes whose source vanished. Fix what your change caused
before moving on; a warning you deliberately leave (e.g. a forward reference
you'll write next) gets a node comment or a memory item so the next session
knows it's intentional. Sync is idempotent and never touches your authored
comments/reviews/metadata.

## Read

- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> list --state ready` — nodes whose dependencies are all closed:
  provable *now*. Other states: `closed`, `blocked`, `formalized_open`.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` — the ready nodes ranked by how many downstream nodes a
  proof would unlock. **Use this when picking the next node to prove.**
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:thm:foo` — one node: statement, `lean_status`
  (`lean_ok | mathlib_ok | sorry | empty`, derived from scanning the Lean, not
  from `\leanok`), deps, attached comments/reviews.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> ancestors label:thm:foo` — the dependency cone.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> stats` — per-state counts for the project.

## Write — per-node progress lives WITH the node

- **Comment = failure memory / progress note on that node.** When an approach
  fails or you learn something node-specific, record it where the next session
  will look first:
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> add comment label:thm:foo --content "tried simp+ring, fails because …"`
  Agent authorship plus run/session/task provenance are filled from the run
  environment; do not copy the note into the blueprint.
- **Review = a Maths / Lean verdict** (independent axes, `good|bad`):
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> add review label:thm:foo --maths good --lean bad --lean-comment "statement ok; proof has a sorry at the succ case"`
- **Metadata**: `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> modify node label:thm:foo --set status=verified`

Prefer node comments over inbox items for anything scoped to ONE node; use the
inbox (skill: `horizon-inbox`) for cross-node or cross-session coordination.

An edge `source --uses--> target` means *source depends on target*. A node is
"ready" when all of its dependencies are closed; prefer `frontier`, which ranks
ready nodes by what they unlock. The dashboard provides the workspace project
switcher and the chapter-collapsed Graphviz view.

## Relation to the blueprint

The DAG **is** the hgraph — there is no second engine and no parser fallback.
It is generated by resolving the blueprint's `\uses{}`/`\lean{}` annotations
against the real Lean sources, so keeping those annotations correct (skill:
`blueprint-conventions`) is exactly what keeps this graph correct. Unresolved
references surface as `horizon graph sync` warnings and as `dangling` entries — read
the warnings rather than trusting `dangling` alone.

    37	def LaurentChartData.pullbackX (D : LaurentChartData Y) (pi : C ⟶ Y) :
    38	    Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₀) :=
    39	  (pi.left.app D.V₀).hom D.x
    40	
    41	/-- The pullback of the second Laurent coordinate to the second source chart. -/
    42	def LaurentChartData.pullbackY (D : LaurentChartData Y) (pi : C ⟶ Y) :
    43	    Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₁) :=
    44	  (pi.left.app D.V₁).hom D.y
    45	
    46	/-- Restriction from the first source chart to the pulled-back overlap. -/
    47	def LaurentChartData.sourceRestriction0 (D : LaurentChartData Y)
    48	    (pi : C ⟶ Y) :
    49	    Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₀) →+*
    50	      Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)) :=
    51	  (C.left.presheaf.map
    52	    (homOfLE (pi.left.preimage_mono
    53	      (inf_le_left : D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₀))).op).hom
    54	
    55	/-- Restriction from the second source chart to the pulled-back overlap. -/
    56	def LaurentChartData.sourceRestriction1 (D : LaurentChartData Y)
    57	    (pi : C ⟶ Y) :
    58	    Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₁) →+*
    59	      Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)) :=
    60	  (C.left.presheaf.map
    61	    (homOfLE (pi.left.preimage_mono
    62	      (inf_le_right : D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₁))).op).hom
    63	
    64	/-- The pulled-back Laurent coordinates remain mutually inverse on the source
    65	overlap. -/
    66	theorem LaurentChartData.sourceRestriction_mul (D : LaurentChartData Y)
    67	    (pi : C ⟶ Y) :
    68	    D.sourceRestriction0 pi (D.pullbackX pi) *
    69	      D.sourceRestriction1 pi (D.pullbackY pi) = 1 := by
    70	  have h0 : D.sourceRestriction0 pi (D.pullbackX pi) =
    71	      (pi.left.app (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)).hom
    72	        ((Y.left.presheaf.map
    73	          (homOfLE (inf_le_left : D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₀)).op).hom D.x) := by
    74	    have h := congrArg
    75	      (fun g : Γ(Y.left, D.V₀) ⟶
    76	          Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)) => g.hom D.x)
    77	      (pi.left.naturality
    78	        (homOfLE (inf_le_left : D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₀)).op)
    79	    exact h.symm
    80	  have h1 : D.sourceRestriction1 pi (D.pullbackY pi) =
    81	      (pi.left.app (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)).hom
    82	        ((Y.left.presheaf.map
    83	          (homOfLE (inf_le_right : D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₁)).op).hom D.y) := by
    84	    have h := congrArg
    85	      (fun g : Γ(Y.left, D.V₁) ⟶
    86	          Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)) => g.hom D.y)
    87	      (pi.left.naturality
    88	        (homOfLE (inf_le_right : D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₁)).op)
    89	    exact h.symm
    90	  rw [h0, h1, ← map_mul, D.res_x_mul_res_y, map_one]
    91	
    92	/-- Aligned source-ring generators for the two pulled-back Laurent charts. -/
    93	structure LaurentChartData.FiniteMapGenerators (D : LaurentChartData Y)
    94	    (pi : C ⟶ Y) : Type u where
    95	  n0 : ℕ
    96	  n1 : ℕ
    97	  d : ℕ
    98	  aa : Fin n0 ⊕ Fin n1 → Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₀)
    99	  bb : Fin n0 ⊕ Fin n1 → Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₁)
   100	  pos : 0 < d
   101	  compatible : ∀ i,
   102	    D.sourceRestriction0 pi (aa i) =
   103	      (D.sourceRestriction0 pi (D.pullbackX pi)) ^ d *
   104	        D.sourceRestriction1 pi (bb i)
   105	  span0 :
   106	    letI : Algebra Γ(Y.left, D.V₀) Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₀) :=
   107	      RingHom.toAlgebra (pi.left.app D.V₀).hom
   108	    Submodule.span Γ(Y.left, D.V₀) (Set.range aa) = ⊤
   109	  span1 :
   110	    letI : Algebra Γ(Y.left, D.V₁) Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₁) :=
   111	      RingHom.toAlgebra (pi.left.app D.V₁).hom
   112	    Submodule.span Γ(Y.left, D.V₁) (Set.range bb) = ⊤
   113	
   114	/-- A finite morphism over Laurent chart data admits aligned finite source
   115	generators after one positive common twist. No projectivity or rational-point
   116	hypothesis is used. -/
   117	theorem LaurentChartData.nonempty_finiteMapGenerators
   118	    (D : LaurentChartData Y) (pi : C ⟶ Y) [IsFinite pi.left] :
   119	    Nonempty (D.FiniteMapGenerators pi) := by
   120	  classical
   121	  letI iA0 : Algebra Γ(Y.left, D.V₀) Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₀) :=
   122	    RingHom.toAlgebra (pi.left.app D.V₀).hom
   123	  letI iA1 : Algebra Γ(Y.left, D.V₁) Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₁) :=
   124	    RingHom.toAlgebra (pi.left.app D.V₁).hom
   125	  letI iA01 : Algebra Γ(Y.left, D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)
   126	      Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)) :=
   127	    RingHom.toAlgebra (pi.left.app (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)).hom
   128	  haveI hfin0 : Module.Finite Γ(Y.left, D.V₀)
   129	      Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₀) :=
   130	    pi.left.finite_app D.V₀ D.isAffineOpen_V₀
   131	  haveI hfin1 : Module.Finite Γ(Y.left, D.V₁)
   132	      Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₁) :=
   133	    pi.left.finite_app D.V₁ D.isAffineOpen_V₁
   134	  let rho0 : Γ(Y.left, D.V₀) →ₐ[ℤ] Γ(Y.left, D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁) :=
   135	    ((Y.left.presheaf.map
   136	      (homOfLE (inf_le_left : D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₀)).op).hom).toIntAlgHom
   137	  let rho1 : Γ(Y.left, D.V₁) →ₐ[ℤ] Γ(Y.left, D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁) :=
   138	    ((Y.left.presheaf.map
   139	      (homOfLE (inf_le_right : D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₁)).op).hom).toIntAlgHom
   140	  let sigma0 : Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₀) →ₗ[ℤ]
   141	      Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)) :=
   142	    (D.sourceRestriction0 pi).toIntAlgHom.toLinearMap
   143	  let sigma1 : Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₁) →ₗ[ℤ]
   144	      Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)) :=
   145	    (D.sourceRestriction1 pi).toIntAlgHom.toLinearMap
   146	  have htu : rho0 D.x * rho1 D.y = 1 := D.res_x_mul_res_y
   147	  have hsigma0 : ∀ (c : Γ(Y.left, D.V₀))
   148	      (m : Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₀)),
   149	      sigma0 (c • m) = rho0 c • sigma0 m := by
   150	    intro c m
   151	    change D.sourceRestriction0 pi ((pi.left.app D.V₀).hom c * m) =
   152	      (pi.left.app (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)).hom (rho0 c) *
   153	        D.sourceRestriction0 pi m
   154	    rw [map_mul]
   155	    congr 1
   156	    have h := congrArg
   157	      (fun g : Γ(Y.left, D.V₀) ⟶
   158	          Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)) => g.hom c)
   159	      (pi.left.naturality
   160	        (homOfLE (inf_le_left : D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₀)).op)
   161	    exact h.symm
   162	  have hsigma1 : ∀ (c : Γ(Y.left, D.V₁))
   163	      (m : Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₁)),
   164	      sigma1 (c • m) = rho1 c • sigma1 m := by
   165	    intro c m
   166	    change D.sourceRestriction1 pi ((pi.left.app D.V₁).hom c * m) =
   167	      (pi.left.app (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)).hom (rho1 c) *
   168	        D.sourceRestriction1 pi m
   169	    rw [map_mul]
   170	    congr 1
   171	    have h := congrArg
   172	      (fun g : Γ(Y.left, D.V₁) ⟶
   173	          Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)) => g.hom c)
   174	      (pi.left.naturality
   175	        (homOfLE (inf_le_right : D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₁)).op)
   176	    exact h.symm
   177	  let t := sigma0 (D.pullbackX pi)
   178	  let u := sigma1 (D.pullbackY pi)
   179	  have hWx : pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁) =
   180	      C.left.basicOpen (D.pullbackX pi) := by
   181	    rw [D.inf_eq_basicOpen_x, Scheme.preimage_basicOpen]
   182	    rfl
   183	  have hWy : pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁) =
   184	      C.left.basicOpen (D.pullbackY pi) := by
   185	    rw [D.inf_eq_basicOpen_y, Scheme.preimage_basicOpen]
   186	    rfl
   187	  have ht : t = (pi.left.app (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)).hom (rho0 D.x) := by
   188	    have h := congrArg
   189	      (fun g : Γ(Y.left, D.V₀) ⟶
   190	          Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)) => g.hom D.x)
   191	      (pi.left.naturality
   192	        (homOfLE (inf_le_left : D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₀)).op)
   193	    exact h.symm
   194	  have hu : u = (pi.left.app (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)).hom (rho1 D.y) := by
   195	    have h := congrArg
   196	      (fun g : Γ(Y.left, D.V₁) ⟶
   197	          Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)) => g.hom D.y)
   198	      (pi.left.naturality
   199	        (homOfLE (inf_le_right : D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₁)).op)
   200	    exact h.symm
   201	  have hext0 : ∀ v : Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)),
   202	      ∃ (n : ℕ) (m : Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₀)),
   203	        rho0 D.x ^ n • v = sigma0 m := by
   204	    intro v
   205	    obtain ⟨n, m, hm⟩ := exists_pow_mul_eq_res
   206	      (D.isAffineOpen_V₀.preimage pi.left) (D.pullbackX pi) hWx
   207	        (pi.left.preimage_mono inf_le_left) v
   208	    refine ⟨n, m, ?_⟩
   209	    change (pi.left.app (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)).hom (rho0 D.x ^ n) * v =
   210	      sigma0 m
   211	    rw [map_pow, ← ht]
   212	    exact hm
   213	  have hext1 : ∀ v : Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)),
   214	      ∃ (n : ℕ) (m : Γ(C.left, pi.left ⁻¹ᵁ D.V₁)),
   215	        rho1 D.y ^ n • v = sigma1 m := by
   216	    intro v
   217	    obtain ⟨n, m, hm⟩ := exists_pow_mul_eq_res
   218	      (D.isAffineOpen_V₁.preimage pi.left) (D.pullbackY pi) hWy
   219	        (pi.left.preimage_mono inf_le_right) v
   220	    refine ⟨n, m, ?_⟩
   221	    change (pi.left.app (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)).hom (rho1 D.y ^ n) * v =
   222	      sigma1 m
   223	    rw [map_pow, ← hu]
   224	    exact hm
   225	  obtain ⟨n0, n1, d, aa, bb, hd, hab, hspan0, hspan1⟩ :=
   226	    AlgebraicJacobian.TwoChart.exists_uniform_twisted_generators
   227	      rho0 rho1 D.x D.y htu sigma0 sigma1 hsigma0 hsigma1 hext0 hext1
   228	  refine ⟨{
   229	    n0 := n0
   230	    n1 := n1
   231	    d := d
   232	    aa := aa
   233	    bb := bb
   234	    pos := hd
   235	    compatible := ?_
   236	    span0 := hspan0
   237	    span1 := hspan1 }⟩
   238	  intro i
   239	  have hi := hab i
   240	  change D.sourceRestriction0 pi (aa i) =
   241	    (pi.left.app (D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁)).hom (rho0 D.x ^ d) *
   242	      D.sourceRestriction1 pi (bb i) at hi
   243	  rw [map_pow, ← ht] at hi
   244	  exact hi
   245	
   246	end AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.P1SectionsFinite
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveCoordinateChart
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Projective coordinates from two aligned Laurent charts
    11	
    12	This file turns the aligned generators produced by
    13	TwoChart.exists_uniform_twisted_generators into homogeneous coordinate
    14	families. For a positive twist d, it adjoins every degree-d base monomial:
    15	
    16	* 1, x, ..., x^d on the first chart;
    17	* y^d, ..., y, 1 on the second chart.
    18	
    19	If t * u = 1 on the overlap and the extra generators satisfy
    20	rho0 (aa i) = t^d * rho1 (bb i), then the complete coordinate families
    21	differ by the common unit t^d. Consequently their normalized affine-chart
    22	maps into the integral Proj agree on the overlap. These are the algebraic
    23	coordinates used to globalize a finite map to the projective line.
    24	-/
    25	
    26	set_option autoImplicit false
    27	
    28	universe u
    29	
    30	open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry
    31	
    32	namespace AlgebraicJacobian.TwoChart.TwistedCoordinates
    33	
    34	variable {I R0 R1 R01 : Type u}
    35	  [CommRing R0] [CommRing R1] [CommRing R01]
    36	
    37	/-- The degree-d base monomials followed by the aligned generators on the
    38	x-chart. -/
    39	def chart0 (d : ℕ) (x : R0) (aa : I → R0) :
    40	    Fin (d + 1) ⊕ I → R0
    41	  | Sum.inl r => x ^ (r : ℕ)
    42	  | Sum.inr i => aa i
    43	
    44	/-- The same degree-d base monomials in reverse order, followed by the
    45	aligned generators on the y-chart. -/
    46	def chart1 (d : ℕ) (y : R1) (bb : I → R1) :
    47	    Fin (d + 1) ⊕ I → R1
    48	  | Sum.inl r => y ^ (d - (r : ℕ))
    49	  | Sum.inr i => bb i
    50	
    51	@[simp]
    52	theorem chart0_inl (d : ℕ) (x : R0) (aa : I → R0)
    53	    (r : Fin (d + 1)) :
    54	    chart0 d x aa (Sum.inl r) = x ^ (r : ℕ) := rfl
    55	
    56	@[simp]
    57	theorem chart0_inr (d : ℕ) (x : R0) (aa : I → R0) (i : I) :
    58	    chart0 d x aa (Sum.inr i) = aa i := rfl
    59	
    60	@[simp]
    61	theorem chart1_inl (d : ℕ) (y : R1) (bb : I → R1)
    62	    (r : Fin (d + 1)) :
    63	    chart1 d y bb (Sum.inl r) = y ^ (d - (r : ℕ)) := rfl
    64	
    65	@[simp]
    66	theorem chart1_inr (d : ℕ) (y : R1) (bb : I → R1) (i : I) :
    67	    chart1 d y bb (Sum.inr i) = bb i := rfl
    68	
    69	/-- The first family is normalized at the degree-d monomial X0^d. -/
    70	@[simp]
    71	theorem chart0_zero (d : ℕ) (x : R0) (aa : I → R0) :
    72	    chart0 d x aa (Sum.inl ⟨0, Nat.zero_lt_succ d⟩) = 1 := by
    73	  simp
    74	
    75	/-- The second family is normalized at the degree-d monomial X1^d. -/
    76	@[simp]
    77	theorem chart1_last (d : ℕ) (y : R1) (bb : I → R1) :
    78	    chart1 d y bb (Sum.inl ⟨d, Nat.lt_succ_self d⟩) = 1 := by
    79	  simp
    80	
    81	/-- A positive twist ensures that the first family contains the base
    82	coordinate x itself, not just the two endpoint monomials. -/
    83	@[simp]
    84	theorem chart0_one (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (x : R0) (aa : I → R0) :
    85	    chart0 d x aa (Sum.inl ⟨1, Nat.succ_lt_succ hd⟩) = x := by
    86	  simp
    87	
    88	/-- The complete chart families differ by the common factor rho0 x ^ d on
    89	the overlap. The base-monomial case is the identity
    90	t^r = t^d * u^(d-r) following from t * u = 1. -/
    91	theorem map_chart (rho0 : R0 →+* R01) (rho1 : R1 →+* R01)
    92	    (x : R0) (y : R1) (htu : rho0 x * rho1 y = 1)
    93	    (d : ℕ) (aa : I → R0) (bb : I → R1)
    94	    (hab : ∀ i, rho0 (aa i) = rho0 x ^ d * rho1 (bb i)) :
    95	    ∀ j, rho0 (chart0 d x aa j) =
    96	      rho0 x ^ d * rho1 (chart1 d y bb j) := by
    97	  rintro (r | i)
    98	  · simp only [chart0_inl, chart1_inl, map_pow]
    99	    have hr : (r : ℕ) + (d - (r : ℕ)) = d :=
   100	      Nat.add_sub_of_le (Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp r.isLt)
   101	    calc
   102	      rho0 x ^ (r : ℕ) =
   103	          rho0 x ^ (r : ℕ) * 1 := (mul_one _).symm
   104	      _ = rho0 x ^ (r : ℕ) *
   105	          (rho0 x * rho1 y) ^ (d - (r : ℕ)) := by
   106	        rw [htu, one_pow]
   107	      _ = rho0 x ^ (r : ℕ) *
   108	          (rho0 x ^ (d - (r : ℕ)) * rho1 y ^ (d - (r : ℕ))) := by
   109	        rw [mul_pow]
   110	      _ = rho0 x ^ d * rho1 y ^ (d - (r : ℕ)) := by
   111	        rw [← mul_assoc, ← pow_add, hr]
   112	  · simpa only [chart0_inr, chart1_inr] using hab i
   113	
   114	/-- The common transition factor is a unit, together with the coordinate
   115	scaling identity it controls. -/
   116	theorem map_chart_unit (rho0 : R0 →+* R01) (rho1 : R1 →+* R01)
   117	    (x : R0) (y : R1) (htu : rho0 x * rho1 y = 1)
   118	    (d : ℕ) (aa : I → R0) (bb : I → R1)
   119	    (hab : ∀ i, rho0 (aa i) = rho0 x ^ d * rho1 (bb i)) :
   120	    IsUnit (rho0 x ^ d) ∧
   121	      ∀ j, rho0 (chart0 d x aa j) =
   122	        rho0 x ^ d * rho1 (chart1 d y bb j) :=
   123	  ⟨(IsUnit.of_mul_eq_one _ htu).pow d,
   124	    map_chart rho0 rho1 x y htu d aa bb hab⟩
   125	
   126	/-- Enlarging a spanning family by the degree-d base monomials preserves
   127	spanning on the first chart. -/
   128	theorem span_chart0 {A : Type u} [Semiring A] [Module A R0]
   129	    (d : ℕ) (x : R0) (aa : I → R0)
   130	    (hspan : Submodule.span A (Set.range aa) = ⊤) :
   131	    Submodule.span A (Set.range (chart0 d x aa)) = ⊤ := by
   132	  apply top_unique
   133	  rw [← hspan]
   134	  apply Submodule.span_mono
   135	  rintro z ⟨i, rfl⟩
   136	  exact ⟨Sum.inr i, rfl⟩
   137	
   138	/-- Enlarging a spanning family by the degree-d base monomials preserves
   139	spanning on the second chart. -/
   140	theorem span_chart1 {A : Type u} [Semiring A] [Module A R1]
   141	    (d : ℕ) (y : R1) (bb : I → R1)
   142	    (hspan : Submodule.span A (Set.range bb) = ⊤) :
   143	    Submodule.span A (Set.range (chart1 d y bb)) = ⊤ := by
   144	  apply top_unique
   145	  rw [← hspan]
   146	  apply Submodule.span_mono
   147	  rintro z ⟨i, rfl⟩
   148	  exact ⟨Sum.inr i, rfl⟩
   149	
   150	/-- The two normalized affine-chart maps into projective space agree after
   151	restriction to the overlap. This is the gluing equation for the finite-map
   152	projective embedding. -/
   153	theorem fromSpec_compat [Finite I]
   154	    (rho0 : R0 →+* R01) (rho1 : R1 →+* R01)
   155	    (x : R0) (y : R1) (htu : rho0 x * rho1 y = 1)
   156	    (d : ℕ) (aa : I → R0) (bb : I → R1)
   157	    (hab : ∀ i, rho0 (aa i) = rho0 x ^ d * rho1 (bb i)) :
   158	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom rho0) ≫
   159	        ProjectiveSpace.Coordinates.fromSpec
   160	          (Sum.inl ⟨0, Nat.zero_lt_succ d⟩) (chart0 d x aa)
   161	          (chart0_zero d x aa) =
   162	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom rho1) ≫
   163	        ProjectiveSpace.Coordinates.fromSpec
   164	          (Sum.inl ⟨d, Nat.lt_succ_self d⟩) (chart1 d y bb)
   165	          (chart1_last d y bb) := by
   166	  rw [ProjectiveSpace.Coordinates.SpecMap_fromSpec,
   167	    ProjectiveSpace.Coordinates.SpecMap_fromSpec]
   168	  apply ProjectiveSpace.Coordinates.fromSpec_eq_of_unit_smul
   169	      (lambda := rho0 x ^ d)
   170	  · exact (IsUnit.of_mul_eq_one _ htu).pow d
   171	  · exact map_chart rho0 rho1 x y htu d aa bb hab
   172	
   173	end AlgebraicJacobian.TwoChart.TwistedCoordinates

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveSpace

     8	/-!
     9	# Projective morphisms
    10	
    11	This file supplies the universe-polymorphic geometric core of projectivity that
    12	Mathlib v4.31 does not yet provide. A morphism is projective when it factors as
    13	a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional relative projective space.
    14	
    15	The line-bundle-carrying refinement used by the Quot construction remains in
    16	`Picard/ProjectiveMorphism.lean`; that refinement is universe-monomorphic because
    17	its Serre twist is built by the project-local sheaf gluing engine.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	open CategoryTheory Limits
    21	
    22	noncomputable section
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    27	
    28	/-- A morphism is projective if it admits a closed immersion into a
    29	finite-dimensional relative projective space over its target. -/
    30	def Scheme.Hom.IsProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (pi : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
    31	  ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    32	    IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi
    33	
    34	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
    35	
    36	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} {pi : X ⟶ S}
    37	
    38	/-- Projective morphisms are proper. -/
    39	theorem isProper (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsProper pi := by
    40	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    41	  letI : Finite n := hn
    42	  haveI := hi
    43	  rw [← hcomp]
    44	  infer_instance
    45	
    46	/-- Projective morphisms are locally of finite type. -/
    47	theorem locallyOfFiniteType (h : pi.IsProjective) : LocallyOfFiniteType pi :=
    48	  haveI := h.isProper
    49	  inferInstance
    50	
    51	/-- Projective morphisms are separated. -/
    52	theorem isSeparated (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsSeparated pi :=
    53	  haveI := h.isProper
    54	  inferInstance
    55	
    56	/-- Projective morphisms are universally closed. -/
    57	theorem universallyClosed (h : pi.IsProjective) : UniversallyClosed pi :=
    58	  haveI := h.isProper
    59	  inferInstance
    60	
    61	/-- A closed immersion into a projective scheme is projective. -/
    62	theorem comp_isClosedImmersion (h : pi.IsProjective) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    63	    (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] : (j ≫ pi).IsProjective := by
    64	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    65	  letI : Finite n := hn
    66	  haveI := hi
    67	  exact ⟨n, hn, j ≫ i, inferInstance, by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp]⟩
    68	
    69	/-- The comparison morphism from the base-changed source to the corresponding
    70	base change of its ambient projective space. -/
    71	private def baseChangeLift {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) {n : Type u}
    72	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) :
    73	    pullback pi g ⟶ ℙ(n; S') :=
    74	  (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).lift
    75	    (pullback.fst pi g ≫ i) (pullback.snd pi g)
    76	    (by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp, pullback.condition])
    77	
    78	/-- Projective morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change. -/
    79	theorem baseChange (h : pi.IsProjective) {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) :
    80	    (pullback.snd pi g).IsProjective := by
    81	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    82	  letI : Finite n := hn
    83	  haveI := hi
    84	  refine ⟨n, hn, baseChangeLift g i hcomp, ?_, ?_⟩
    85	  · have h1 : baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S') =
    86	        pullback.snd pi g := IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
    87	    have hsq : IsPullback (baseChangeLift g i hcomp) (pullback.fst pi g)
    88	        (ProjectiveSpace.map n g) i := by
    89	      have hbig : IsPullback
    90	          (baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S'))
    91	          (pullback.fst pi g) g (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := by
    92	        rw [h1, hcomp]
    93	        exact (IsPullback.of_hasPullback pi g).flip
    94	      exact IsPullback.of_right hbig
    95	        (IsPullback.lift_fst _ _ _ _)
    96	        (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).flip
    97	    exact MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip hi
    98	  · exact IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
    99	
   100	end Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
   101	
   102	namespace ProjectiveSpace
   103	
   104	/-- The structural morphism of relative projective space is projective. -/
   105	theorem isProjective_over (n : Type u) [Finite n] (S : Scheme.{u}) :
   106	    (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S).IsProjective :=
   107	  ⟨n, inferInstance, 𝟙 _, inferInstance, Category.id_comp _⟩
   108	
   109	end ProjectiveSpace
   110	
   111	end AlgebraicGeometry

    14	/-!
    15	# Finite-morphism embeddings
    16	
    17	This file supplies two pieces of the standard proof that finite morphisms are
    18	projective. Over an affine target, a finite morphism is a closed subscheme of
    19	finite-dimensional affine space. At the other end of the compactification
    20	argument, a proper immersion into projective space is already closed.
    21	
    22	The remaining geometric step is to place the affine embedding in a projective
    23	chart and globalize it over the target. These results isolate both sides of
    24	that step without adding a projectivity hypothesis.
    25	-/
    26	
    27	open CategoryTheory Limits MvPolynomial
    28	
    29	noncomputable section
    30	
    31	universe u
    32	
    33	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    34	
    35	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
    36	
    37	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} {pi : X ⟶ S}
    38	
    39	/-- A proper morphism that factors through projective space by an immersion is
    40	projective. Properness makes the immersion closed. -/
    41	theorem of_isProper_of_immersion (hpi : IsProper pi) {n : Type u} [Finite n]
    42	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hi : IsImmersion i)
    43	    (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) : pi.IsProjective := by
    44	  letI : IsImmersion i := hi
    45	  haveI : IsProper (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := hcomp ▸ hpi
    46	  haveI : IsProper i := IsProper.of_comp i (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)
    47	  haveI : IsClosedImmersion i :=
    48	    (IsClosedImmersion.iff_isProper_and_mono (f := i)).mpr
    49	      ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩
    50	  exact ⟨n, inferInstance, i, inferInstance, hcomp⟩
    51	
    52	end Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
    53	
    54	namespace IsFinite
    55	
    56	/-- A specified finite module-spanning family in the affine source ring
    57	defines a closed immersion into affine space over the base. This is the
    58	chosen-generator form of `exists_closedImmersion_affineSpace`, used when the
    59	generators on two base charts have already been aligned. -/
    60	theorem isClosedImmersion_homOfVector_of_span_eq_top
    61	    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y]
    62	    {n : Type u} [Finite n] (a : n → Γ(X, ⊤))
    63	    (hspan :
    64	      letI : Algebra Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) := RingHom.toAlgebra f.appTop.hom
    65	      Submodule.span Γ(Y, ⊤) (Set.range a) = ⊤) :
    66	    IsClosedImmersion (AffineSpace.homOfVector f a) := by
    67	  classical
    68	  letI : Fintype n := Fintype.ofFinite n
    69	  letI : Algebra Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) := RingHom.toAlgebra f.appTop.hom
    70	  let i : X ⟶ 𝔸(n; Y) := AffineSpace.homOfVector f a
    71	  have hsurj : Function.Surjective (Fintype.linearCombination Γ(Y, ⊤) a) := by
    72	    rw [← LinearMap.range_eq_top, Fintype.range_linearCombination, hspan]
    73	  apply IsClosedImmersion.of_surjective_of_isAffine
    74	  intro x
    75	  obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := hsurj x
    76	  let p : MvPolynomial n Γ(Y, ⊤) :=
    77	    ∑ j, C (c j) * MvPolynomial.X j
    78	  refine ⟨(AffineSpace.isoOfIsAffine n Y).hom.appTop
    79	    ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of (MvPolynomial n Γ(Y, ⊤)))).inv p), ?_⟩
    80	  rw [AffineSpace.isoOfIsAffine_hom_appTop]
    81	  simp only [CommRingCat.comp_apply, Iso.inv_hom_id_apply]
    82	  change (i.appTop.hom.comp
    83	    (eval₂Hom (𝔸(n; Y) ↘ Y).appTop.hom (AffineSpace.coord Y))) p =
    84	      Fintype.linearCombination Γ(Y, ⊤) a c
    85	  have heval :
    86	      i.appTop.hom.comp
    87	        (eval₂Hom (𝔸(n; Y) ↘ Y).appTop.hom (AffineSpace.coord Y)) =
    88	        eval₂Hom f.appTop.hom a := by
    89	    apply MvPolynomial.ringHom_ext
    90	    · intro r
    91	      simp only [RingHom.comp_apply, eval₂Hom_C]
    92	      have h := congrArg Scheme.Hom.appTop
    93	        (AffineSpace.homOfVector_over f a)
    94	      rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop] at h
    95	      exact congrArg (fun e : Γ(Y, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤) => e.hom r) h
    96	    · intro j
    97	      simp [i]
    98	  rw [heval, Fintype.linearCombination_apply]
    99	  simp only [p, map_sum, map_mul, coe_eval₂Hom, eval₂_C, eval₂_X,
   100	    Algebra.smul_def]
   101	  change (∑ x, f.appTop.hom (c x) * a x) =
   102	    ∑ x, f.appTop.hom (c x) * a x
   103	  rfl
   104	
   105	/-- A finite morphism over an affine target is a closed subscheme of a
   106	finite-dimensional affine space over that target. -/
   107	theorem exists_closedImmersion_affineSpace {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
   108	    [IsFinite f] [IsAffine Y] :
   109	    ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ 𝔸(n; Y)),
   110	      IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ (𝔸(n; Y) ↘ Y) = f := by
   111	  letI : IsAffine X := isAffine_of_isAffineHom f
   112	  letI : Algebra Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) := RingHom.toAlgebra f.appTop.hom
   113	  haveI : Module.Finite Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) := f.finite_appTop
   114	  obtain ⟨n, hn, q, hq⟩ :=
   115	    Algebra.FiniteType.iff_quotient_mvPolynomial'.mp
   116	      (inferInstance : Algebra.FiniteType Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤))
   117	  letI : Fintype n := hn
   118	  let i : X ⟶ 𝔸(n; Y) :=
   119	    AffineSpace.homOfVector f fun j => q (MvPolynomial.X j)
   120	  refine ⟨n, inferInstance, i, ?_, AffineSpace.homOfVector_over _ _⟩
   121	  apply IsClosedImmersion.of_surjective_of_isAffine
   122	  intro x
   123	  obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := hq x
   124	  refine ⟨(AffineSpace.isoOfIsAffine n Y).hom.appTop
   125	    ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of (MvPolynomial n Γ(Y, ⊤)))).inv p), ?_⟩
   126	  rw [AffineSpace.isoOfIsAffine_hom_appTop]
   127	  simp only [CommRingCat.comp_apply, Iso.inv_hom_id_apply]
   128	  change (i.appTop.hom.comp
   129	    (eval₂Hom (𝔸(n; Y) ↘ Y).appTop.hom (AffineSpace.coord Y))) p = q.toRingHom p
   130	  apply DFunLike.congr_fun ?_ p
   131	  apply MvPolynomial.ringHom_ext
   132	  · intro r
   133	    simp only [RingHom.comp_apply, eval₂Hom_C]
   134	    rw [show q.toRingHom (C r) = f.appTop.hom r by
   135	      change q (C r) = f.appTop.hom r
   136	      exact q.commutes r]
   137	    have h := congrArg Scheme.Hom.appTop (AffineSpace.homOfVector_over f
   138	      (fun j => q (MvPolynomial.X j)))
   139	    rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop] at h
   140	    exact congrArg (fun e : Γ(Y, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤) => e.hom r) h
   141	  · intro j
   142	    simp [i]
   143	
   144	/-- A finite morphism to an affine target is projective. The affine embedding
   145	lands in the standard open chart of projective space, and properness turns the
   146	resulting immersion into a closed immersion. -/
   147	theorem isProjective_of_isAffine {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
   148	    [IsFinite f] [IsAffine Y] : f.IsProjective := by
   149	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hif⟩ := exists_closedImmersion_affineSpace f
   150	  letI : Finite n := hn
   151	  letI : IsClosedImmersion i := hi
   152	  let j : X ⟶ ℙ(Option n; Y) :=
   153	    i ≫ ProjectiveSpace.standardOpenImmersion n Y
   154	  have hj : IsImmersion j := by
   155	    dsimp [j]
   156	    infer_instance
   157	  apply Scheme.Hom.IsProjective.of_isProper_of_immersion
   158	    (pi := f) (by infer_instance) j hj
   159	  dsimp [j]
   160	  rw [Category.assoc, ProjectiveSpace.standardOpenImmersion_over, hif]
   161	
   162	end IsFinite
   163	
   164	end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveSpace
     7	import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.BigOperators
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Projective coordinate charts
    11	
    12	This file gives the coordinate-level API for constructing morphisms from an
    13	affine scheme to the integral model of projective space. A coordinate family
    14	with one coordinate equal to `1` defines a morphism through the corresponding
    15	standard chart. Two such morphisms agree when their coordinate families differ
    16	by multiplication by a unit.
    17	
    18	The construction is deliberately independent of curves. It is the reusable
    19	gluing substrate for globalizing affine embeddings over the two standard
    20	charts of the projective line.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open CategoryTheory MvPolynomial HomogeneousLocalization
    24	
    25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace.Coordinates
    30	
    31	variable {J : Type u}
    32	variable {B B' : Type u} [CommRing B] [CommRing B']
    33	
    34	/-- Evaluation of the integral homogeneous coordinate ring at a family of
    35	elements of a ring. -/
    36	def eval (c : J → B) : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ) →+* B :=
    37	  eval₂Hom ((Int.castRingHom B).comp
    38	    (ULift.ringEquiv : ULift.{u} ℤ ≃+* ℤ).toRingHom) c
    39	
    40	@[simp]
    41	theorem eval_X (c : J → B) (i : J) : eval c (X i) = c i := by
    42	  simp [eval]
    43	
    44	@[simp]
    45	theorem eval_monomial (c : J → B) (d : J →₀ ℕ) (a : ULift.{u} ℤ) :
    46	    eval c (monomial d a) = (a.down : B) * d.prod (fun i e ↦ c i ^ e) := by
    47	  simp [eval, ULift.ringEquiv]
    48	
    49	/-- A homogeneous polynomial of degree `m` scales by `lambda ^ m` when all
    50	projective coordinates are scaled by `lambda`. -/
    51	theorem eval_smul_of_isHomogeneous [Finite J] (lambda : B) (c : J → B)
    52	    {p : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)} {m : ℕ} (hp : p.IsHomogeneous m) :
    53	    eval (fun i ↦ lambda * c i) p = lambda ^ m * eval c p := by
    54	  classical
    55	  letI := Fintype.ofFinite J
    56	  conv_lhs => rw [p.as_sum]
    57	  conv_rhs => rw [p.as_sum]
    58	  rw [map_sum, map_sum, Finset.mul_sum]
    59	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun d hd ↦ ?_
    60	  have hdeg : Finsupp.degree d = m := by
    61	    by_contra hne
    62	    exact (mem_support_iff.mp hd) (hp.coeff_eq_zero hne)
    63	  rw [eval_monomial, eval_monomial]
    64	  simp_rw [mul_pow]
    65	  rw [Finsupp.prod_mul]
    66	  have hpow : d.prod (fun _ e ↦ lambda ^ e) = lambda ^ m := by
    67	    rw [Finsupp.prod_fintype _ _ (fun _ ↦ pow_zero _),
    68	      Finset.prod_pow_eq_pow_sum, ← Finsupp.degree_eq_sum, hdeg]
    69	  rw [hpow]
    70	  ring
    71	
    72	/-- The lift of a homogeneous-coordinate evaluation to the degree-zero
    73	localization at a homogeneous element whose image is a unit. -/
    74	def awayLift (f : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ))
    75	    (psi : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ) →+* B) (hu : IsUnit (psi f)) :
    76	    Away (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) f →+* B :=
    77	  (IsLocalization.Away.lift (S := Localization.Away f) f hu).comp
    78	    (algebraMap (Away (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) f)
    79	      (Localization.Away f))
    80	
    81	/-- Normal form for `awayLift`: the value of `a / f ^ n`, multiplied by
    82	the evaluated denominator, is the value of `a`. -/
    83	theorem awayLift_mul_eq {f : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)} {e : ℕ}
    84	    (hf : f ∈ homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) e)
    85	    (psi : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ) →+* B)
    86	    (hu : IsUnit (psi f)) (n : ℕ) (a : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ))
    87	    (ha : a ∈ homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) (n • e)) :
    88	    awayLift f psi hu
    89	        (Away.mk (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) hf n a ha) *
    90	      psi f ^ n = psi a := by
    91	  have hspec :
    92	      Localization.mk a (⟨f ^ n, n, rfl⟩ : Submonoid.powers f) *
    93	          algebraMap _ (Localization.Away f) (f ^ n) =
    94	        algebraMap _ (Localization.Away f) a := by
    95	    rw [Localization.mk_eq_mk'_apply]
    96	    exact IsLocalization.mk'_spec _ _ _
    97	  have hlift := congrArg (IsLocalization.Away.lift
    98	    (S := Localization.Away f) f hu) hspec
    99	  rw [map_mul, IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq,
   100	    IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq] at hlift
   101	  calc
   102	    awayLift f psi hu
   103	        (Away.mk (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) hf n a ha) *
   104	      psi f ^ n =
   105	        IsLocalization.Away.lift (S := Localization.Away f) f hu
   106	            (Localization.mk a (⟨f ^ n, n, rfl⟩ : Submonoid.powers f)) *
   107	          psi (f ^ n) := by
   108	      rw [awayLift, RingHom.comp_apply, HomogeneousLocalization.algebraMap_apply,
   109	        HomogeneousLocalization.Away.val_mk, map_pow]
   110	    _ = psi a := hlift
   111	
   112	/-- `awayLift` only depends on the underlying evaluation map. -/
   113	theorem awayLift_congr {f : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)}
   114	    {psi₁ psi₂ : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ) →+* B} (h : psi₁ = psi₂)
   115	    (hu : IsUnit (psi₁ f)) :
   116	    awayLift f psi₁ hu = awayLift f psi₂ (h ▸ hu) := by
   117	  subst h
   118	  rfl
   119	
   120	/-- Post-composition commutes with evaluation. -/
   121	theorem comp_eval (r : B →+* B') (c : J → B) :
   122	    r.comp (eval c) = eval (fun i ↦ r (c i)) := by
   123	  apply MvPolynomial.ringHom_ext
   124	  · intro z
   125	    simp [eval]
   126	  · intro i
   127	    simp
   128	
   129	/-- Post-composition commutes with `awayLift`. -/
   130	theorem comp_awayLift {f : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)} {e : ℕ}
   131	    (hf : f ∈ homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) e) (r : B →+* B')
   132	    (psi : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ) →+* B) (hu : IsUnit (psi f)) :
   133	    r.comp (awayLift f psi hu) =
   134	      awayLift f (r.comp psi) (by simpa using hu.map r) := by
   135	  apply RingHom.ext
   136	  intro w
   137	  obtain ⟨n, a, ha, rfl⟩ :=
   138	    Away.mk_surjective (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) hf w
   139	  have h₁ := congrArg r (awayLift_mul_eq hf psi hu n a ha)
   140	  rw [map_mul, map_pow] at h₁
   141	  have h₂ := awayLift_mul_eq hf (r.comp psi)
   142	    (by simpa using hu.map r) n a ha
   143	  simp only [RingHom.comp_apply] at h₂ ⊢
   144	  exact ((hu.map r).pow n).mul_right_cancel (h₁.trans h₂.symm)
   145	
   146	/-- Every homogeneous coordinate has degree one. -/
   147	theorem X_mem_deg_one (i : J) :
   148	    (X i : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) ∈
   149	      homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) 1 :=
   150	  isHomogeneous_X _ _
   151	
   152	/-- A coordinate family with its `i`-th coordinate equal to one defines a
   153	ring map from the `i`-th standard projective chart. -/
   154	def chartHom (i : J) (c : J → B) (hi : c i = 1) :
   155	    Away (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X i) →+* B :=
   156	  awayLift (X i) (eval c) (by rw [eval_X, hi]; exact isUnit_one)
   157	
   158	/-- Post-composition commutes with a standard-chart classifying map. -/
   159	theorem comp_chartHom (r : B →+* B') (i : J) (c : J → B) (hi : c i = 1) :
   160	    r.comp (chartHom i c hi) =
   161	      chartHom i (fun j ↦ r (c j)) (by rw [hi, map_one]) := by
   162	  rw [chartHom, chartHom]
   163	  exact (comp_awayLift (X_mem_deg_one i) r (eval c)
   164	    (by rw [eval_X, hi]; exact isUnit_one)).trans
   165	      (awayLift_congr (comp_eval r c) _)
   166	
   167	theorem chartHom_mk (i : J) (c : J → B) (hi : c i = 1)
   168	    {e : ℕ} (hf : (X i : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) ∈
   169	      homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) e)
   170	    (n : ℕ) (a : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ))
   171	    (ha : a ∈ homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) (n • e)) :
   172	    chartHom i c hi
   173	      (Away.mk (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) hf n a ha) = eval c a := by
   174	  have h := awayLift_mul_eq hf (eval c)
   175	    (by rw [eval_X, hi]; exact isUnit_one) n a ha
   176	  simpa [chartHom, hi] using h
   177	
   178	/-- The affine morphism into the `i`-th standard chart classified by a
   179	coordinate family whose `i`-th coordinate is one. -/
   180	def fromSpec (i : J) (c : J → B) (hi : c i = 1) :
   181	    Spec (.of B) ⟶ Proj (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) :=
   182	  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (chartHom i c hi)) ≫
   183	    Proj.awayι (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ))
   184	      (X i) (X_mem_deg_one i) Nat.zero_lt_one
   185	
   186	/-- `fromSpec` is natural in the affine coordinate ring. -/
   187	theorem SpecMap_fromSpec (r : B →+* B') (i : J) (c : J → B)
   188	    (hi : c i = 1) :
   189	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom r) ≫ fromSpec i c hi =
   190	      fromSpec i (fun j ↦ r (c j)) (by rw [hi, map_one]) := by
   191	  rw [fromSpec, fromSpec, ← Category.assoc, ← Spec.map_comp]
   192	  congr 2
   193	  ext w
   194	  exact DFunLike.congr_fun (comp_chartHom r i c hi) w
   195	
   196	/-- The product of two degree-one coordinates has degree two. -/
   197	theorem X_mul_X_mem_deg_two (i j : J) :
   198	    (X i * X j : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) ∈
   199	      homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) 2 := by
   200	  simpa using SetLike.mul_mem_graded (X_mem_deg_one i) (X_mem_deg_one j)
   201	
   202	/-- Coordinate maps through two standard charts agree when their coordinate
   203	families differ by multiplication by a unit. -/
   204	theorem fromSpec_eq_of_unit_smul [Finite J] (i₀ i₁ : J) (c₀ c₁ : J → B)
   205	    (hi₀ : c₀ i₀ = 1) (hi₁ : c₁ i₁ = 1) (lambda : B)
   206	    (hlambda : IsUnit lambda) (hc : ∀ j, c₀ j = lambda * c₁ j) :
   207	    fromSpec i₀ c₀ hi₀ = fromSpec i₁ c₁ hi₁ := by
   208	  classical
   209	  letI := Fintype.ofFinite J
   210	  have hc₀i₁ : c₀ i₁ = lambda := by rw [hc i₁, hi₁, mul_one]
   211	  have hunit₀ : IsUnit (c₀ i₁) := by simpa [hc₀i₁] using hlambda
   212	  have hlambda_mul : lambda * c₁ i₀ = 1 := by rw [← hc i₀, hi₀]
   213	  have hunit₁ : IsUnit (c₁ i₀) :=
   214	    IsUnit.of_mul_eq_one _ (by rwa [mul_comm] at hlambda_mul)
   215	  have hu₀ : IsUnit (eval c₀ (X i₀ * X i₁)) := by
   216	    rw [map_mul, eval_X, eval_X, hi₀, one_mul]
   217	    exact hunit₀
   218	  have hu₁ : IsUnit (eval c₁ (X i₀ * X i₁)) := by
   219	    rw [map_mul, eval_X, eval_X, hi₁, mul_one]
   220	    exact hunit₁
   221	  let overlap₀ :
   222	      Away (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X i₀ * X i₁) →+* B :=
   223	    awayLift (X i₀ * X i₁) (eval c₀) hu₀
   224	  let overlap₁ :
   225	      Away (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X i₀ * X i₁) →+* B :=
   226	    awayLift (X i₀ * X i₁) (eval c₁) hu₁
   227	  have hoverlap : overlap₀ = overlap₁ := by
   228	    apply RingHom.ext
   229	    intro w
   230	    obtain ⟨n, a, ha, rfl⟩ := Away.mk_surjective
   231	      (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ))
   232	      (X_mul_X_mem_deg_two i₀ i₁) w
   233	    have h₀ := awayLift_mul_eq (X_mul_X_mem_deg_two i₀ i₁)
   234	      (eval c₀) hu₀ n a ha
   235	    have h₁ := awayLift_mul_eq (X_mul_X_mem_deg_two i₀ i₁)
   236	      (eval c₁) hu₁ n a ha
   237	    have hscale := eval_smul_of_isHomogeneous lambda c₁
   238	      ((mem_homogeneousSubmodule _ _).mp ha)
   239	    have hcoords : c₀ = fun j ↦ lambda * c₁ j := funext hc
   240	    rw [← hcoords] at hscale
   241	    have hexp : n • (2 : ℕ) = 2 * n := by
   242	      rw [Nat.nsmul_eq_mul, Nat.mul_comm]
   243	    rw [hexp] at hscale
   244	    have hden : eval c₀ (X i₀ * X i₁) =
   245	        lambda ^ 2 * eval c₁ (X i₀ * X i₁) := by
   246	      rw [map_mul, map_mul, eval_X, eval_X, eval_X, eval_X, hc i₀, hc i₁]
   247	      ring
   248	    have hcommon : IsUnit
   249	        (lambda ^ (2 * n) * eval c₁ (X i₀ * X i₁) ^ n) :=
   250	      (hlambda.pow (2 * n)).mul (hu₁.pow n)
   251	    apply hcommon.mul_right_cancel
   252	    calc
   253	      overlap₀
   254	            (Away.mk (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ))
   255	              (X_mul_X_mem_deg_two i₀ i₁) n a ha) *
   256	          (lambda ^ (2 * n) * eval c₁ (X i₀ * X i₁) ^ n) =
   257	          overlap₀
   258	              (Away.mk (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ))
   259	                (X_mul_X_mem_deg_two i₀ i₁) n a ha) *
   260	            eval c₀ (X i₀ * X i₁) ^ n := by
   261	              rw [hden, mul_pow, pow_mul]
   262	      _ = eval c₀ a := h₀
   263	      _ = lambda ^ (2 * n) * eval c₁ a := hscale
   264	      _ = lambda ^ (2 * n) *
   265	          (overlap₁
   266	              (Away.mk (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ))
   267	                (X_mul_X_mem_deg_two i₀ i₁) n a ha) *
   268	            eval c₁ (X i₀ * X i₁) ^ n) := by rw [h₁]
   269	      _ = overlap₁
   270	            (Away.mk (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ))
   271	              (X_mul_X_mem_deg_two i₀ i₁) n a ha) *
   272	          (lambda ^ (2 * n) * eval c₁ (X i₀ * X i₁) ^ n) := by ring
   273	  have hfac₀ : overlap₀.comp
   274	        (awayMap (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ))
   275	          (X_mem_deg_one i₁) rfl) = chartHom i₀ c₀ hi₀ := by
   276	    apply RingHom.ext
   277	    intro w
   278	    obtain ⟨n, a, ha, rfl⟩ := Away.mk_surjective
   279	      (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X_mem_deg_one i₀) w
   280	    rw [RingHom.comp_apply, awayMap_mk, chartHom_mk]
   281	    have hmem : a * X i₁ ^ n ∈
   282	        homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) (n • (1 + 1)) := by
   283	      have h := SetLike.mul_mem_graded ha
   284	        (SetLike.pow_mem_graded n (X_mem_deg_one i₁))
   285	      rwa [← smul_add] at h
   286	    have h := awayLift_mul_eq (X_mul_X_mem_deg_two i₀ i₁)
   287	      (eval c₀) hu₀ n (a * X i₁ ^ n) (by simpa using hmem)
   288	    simp only [map_mul, map_pow, eval_X, hi₀, one_mul] at h
   289	    exact (hunit₀.pow n).mul_right_cancel h
   290	  have hfac₁ : overlap₁.comp
   291	        (awayMap (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ))
   292	          (X_mem_deg_one i₀) (mul_comm (X i₀) (X i₁))) =
   293	      chartHom i₁ c₁ hi₁ := by
   294	    apply RingHom.ext
   295	    intro w
   296	    obtain ⟨n, a, ha, rfl⟩ := Away.mk_surjective
   297	      (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X_mem_deg_one i₁) w
   298	    rw [RingHom.comp_apply, awayMap_mk, chartHom_mk]
   299	    have hmem : a * X i₀ ^ n ∈
   300	        homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) (n • (1 + 1)) := by
   301	      have h := SetLike.mul_mem_graded ha
   302	        (SetLike.pow_mem_graded n (X_mem_deg_one i₀))
   303	      rwa [← smul_add] at h
   304	    have h := awayLift_mul_eq (X_mul_X_mem_deg_two i₀ i₁)
   305	      (eval c₁) hu₁ n (a * X i₀ ^ n) (by simpa using hmem)
   306	    simp only [map_mul, map_pow, eval_X, hi₁, mul_one] at h
   307	    exact (hunit₁.pow n).mul_right_cancel h
   308	  rw [fromSpec, fromSpec, ← hfac₀, ← hfac₁,
   309	    CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, Spec.map_comp, Spec.map_comp]
   310	  simp only [Category.assoc]
   311	  rw [Proj.SpecMap_awayMap_awayι, Proj.SpecMap_awayMap_awayι, hoverlap]
   312	
   313	end AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace.Coordinates

    14	/-!
    15	# Finite-morphism embeddings
    16	
    17	This file supplies two pieces of the standard proof that finite morphisms are
    18	projective. Over an affine target, a finite morphism is a closed subscheme of
    19	finite-dimensional affine space. At the other end of the compactification
    20	argument, a proper immersion into projective space is already closed.
    21	
    22	The remaining geometric step is to place the affine embedding in a projective
    23	chart and globalize it over the target. These results isolate both sides of
    24	that step without adding a projectivity hypothesis.
    25	-/
    26	
    27	open CategoryTheory Limits MvPolynomial
    28	
    29	noncomputable section
    30	
    31	universe u
    32	
    33	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    34	
    35	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
    36	
    37	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} {pi : X ⟶ S}
    38	
    39	/-- A proper morphism that factors through projective space by an immersion is
    40	projective. Properness makes the immersion closed. -/
    41	theorem of_isProper_of_immersion (hpi : IsProper pi) {n : Type u} [Finite n]
    42	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hi : IsImmersion i)
    43	    (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) : pi.IsProjective := by
    44	  letI : IsImmersion i := hi
    45	  haveI : IsProper (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := hcomp ▸ hpi
    46	  haveI : IsProper i := IsProper.of_comp i (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)
    47	  haveI : IsClosedImmersion i :=
    48	    (IsClosedImmersion.iff_isProper_and_mono (f := i)).mpr
    49	      ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩
    50	  exact ⟨n, inferInstance, i, inferInstance, hcomp⟩
    51	
    52	end Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
    53	
    54	namespace IsFinite
    55	
    56	/-- A specified finite module-spanning family in the affine source ring
    57	defines a closed immersion into affine space over the base. This is the
    58	chosen-generator form of `exists_closedImmersion_affineSpace`, used when the
    59	generators on two base charts have already been aligned. -/
    60	theorem isClosedImmersion_homOfVector_of_span_eq_top
    61	    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y]
    62	    {n : Type u} [Finite n] (a : n → Γ(X, ⊤))
    63	    (hspan :
    64	      letI : Algebra Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) := RingHom.toAlgebra f.appTop.hom
    65	      Submodule.span Γ(Y, ⊤) (Set.range a) = ⊤) :
    66	    IsClosedImmersion (AffineSpace.homOfVector f a) := by
    67	  classical
    68	  letI : Fintype n := Fintype.ofFinite n
    69	  letI : Algebra Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) := RingHom.toAlgebra f.appTop.hom
    70	  let i : X ⟶ 𝔸(n; Y) := AffineSpace.homOfVector f a
    71	  have hsurj : Function.Surjective (Fintype.linearCombination Γ(Y, ⊤) a) := by
    72	    rw [← LinearMap.range_eq_top, Fintype.range_linearCombination, hspan]
    73	  apply IsClosedImmersion.of_surjective_of_isAffine
    74	  intro x
    75	  obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := hsurj x
    76	  let p : MvPolynomial n Γ(Y, ⊤) :=
    77	    ∑ j, C (c j) * MvPolynomial.X j
    78	  refine ⟨(AffineSpace.isoOfIsAffine n Y).hom.appTop
    79	    ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of (MvPolynomial n Γ(Y, ⊤)))).inv p), ?_⟩
    80	  rw [AffineSpace.isoOfIsAffine_hom_appTop]
    81	  simp only [CommRingCat.comp_apply, Iso.inv_hom_id_apply]
    82	  change (i.appTop.hom.comp
    83	    (eval₂Hom (𝔸(n; Y) ↘ Y).appTop.hom (AffineSpace.coord Y))) p =
    84	      Fintype.linearCombination Γ(Y, ⊤) a c
    85	  have heval :
    86	      i.appTop.hom.comp
    87	        (eval₂Hom (𝔸(n; Y) ↘ Y).appTop.hom (AffineSpace.coord Y)) =
    88	        eval₂Hom f.appTop.hom a := by
    89	    apply MvPolynomial.ringHom_ext
    90	    · intro r
    91	      simp only [RingHom.comp_apply, eval₂Hom_C]
    92	      have h := congrArg Scheme.Hom.appTop
    93	        (AffineSpace.homOfVector_over f a)
    94	      rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop] at h
    95	      exact congrArg (fun e : Γ(Y, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤) => e.hom r) h
    96	    · intro j
    97	      simp [i]
    98	  rw [heval, Fintype.linearCombination_apply]
    99	  simp only [p, map_sum, map_mul, coe_eval₂Hom, eval₂_C, eval₂_X,
   100	    Algebra.smul_def]
   101	  change (∑ x, f.appTop.hom (c x) * a x) =
   102	    ∑ x, f.appTop.hom (c x) * a x
   103	  rfl
   104	
   105	/-- A finite morphism over an affine target is a closed subscheme of a
   106	finite-dimensional affine space over that target. -/
   107	theorem exists_closedImmersion_affineSpace {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
   108	    [IsFinite f] [IsAffine Y] :
   109	    ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ 𝔸(n; Y)),
   110	      IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ (𝔸(n; Y) ↘ Y) = f := by
   111	  letI : IsAffine X := isAffine_of_isAffineHom f
   112	  letI : Algebra Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) := RingHom.toAlgebra f.appTop.hom
   113	  haveI : Module.Finite Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤) := f.finite_appTop
   114	  obtain ⟨n, hn, q, hq⟩ :=
   115	    Algebra.FiniteType.iff_quotient_mvPolynomial'.mp
   116	      (inferInstance : Algebra.FiniteType Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(X, ⊤))
   117	  letI : Fintype n := hn
   118	  let i : X ⟶ 𝔸(n; Y) :=
   119	    AffineSpace.homOfVector f fun j => q (MvPolynomial.X j)
   120	  refine ⟨n, inferInstance, i, ?_, AffineSpace.homOfVector_over _ _⟩
   121	  apply IsClosedImmersion.of_surjective_of_isAffine
   122	  intro x
   123	  obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := hq x
   124	  refine ⟨(AffineSpace.isoOfIsAffine n Y).hom.appTop
   125	    ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of (MvPolynomial n Γ(Y, ⊤)))).inv p), ?_⟩
   126	  rw [AffineSpace.isoOfIsAffine_hom_appTop]
   127	  simp only [CommRingCat.comp_apply, Iso.inv_hom_id_apply]
   128	  change (i.appTop.hom.comp
   129	    (eval₂Hom (𝔸(n; Y) ↘ Y).appTop.hom (AffineSpace.coord Y))) p = q.toRingHom p
   130	  apply DFunLike.congr_fun ?_ p
   131	  apply MvPolynomial.ringHom_ext
   132	  · intro r
   133	    simp only [RingHom.comp_apply, eval₂Hom_C]
   134	    rw [show q.toRingHom (C r) = f.appTop.hom r by
   135	      change q (C r) = f.appTop.hom r
   136	      exact q.commutes r]
   137	    have h := congrArg Scheme.Hom.appTop (AffineSpace.homOfVector_over f
   138	      (fun j => q (MvPolynomial.X j)))
   139	    rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop] at h
   140	    exact congrArg (fun e : Γ(Y, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤) => e.hom r) h
   141	  · intro j
   142	    simp [i]
   143	
   144	/-- A finite morphism to an affine target is projective. The affine embedding
   145	lands in the standard open chart of projective space, and properness turns the
   146	resulting immersion into a closed immersion. -/
   147	theorem isProjective_of_isAffine {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
   148	    [IsFinite f] [IsAffine Y] : f.IsProjective := by
   149	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hif⟩ := exists_closedImmersion_affineSpace f
   150	  letI : Finite n := hn
   151	  letI : IsClosedImmersion i := hi
   152	  let j : X ⟶ ℙ(Option n; Y) :=
   153	    i ≫ ProjectiveSpace.standardOpenImmersion n Y
   154	  have hj : IsImmersion j := by
   155	    dsimp [j]
   156	    infer_instance
   157	  apply Scheme.Hom.IsProjective.of_isProper_of_immersion
   158	    (pi := f) (by infer_instance) j hj
   159	  dsimp [j]
   160	  rw [Category.assoc, ProjectiveSpace.standardOpenImmersion_over, hif]
   161	
   162	end IsFinite
   163	
   164	end AlgebraicGeometry

     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Projective coordinates from two aligned Laurent charts
    11	
    12	This file turns the aligned generators produced by
    13	TwoChart.exists_uniform_twisted_generators into homogeneous coordinate
    14	families. For a positive twist d, it adjoins every degree-d base monomial:
    15	
    16	* 1, x, ..., x^d on the first chart;
    17	* y^d, ..., y, 1 on the second chart.
    18	
    19	If t * u = 1 on the overlap and the extra generators satisfy
    20	rho0 (aa i) = t^d * rho1 (bb i), then the complete coordinate families
    21	differ by the common unit t^d. Consequently their normalized affine-chart
    22	maps into the integral Proj agree on the overlap. These are the algebraic
    23	coordinates used to globalize a finite map to the projective line.
    24	-/
    25	
    26	set_option autoImplicit false
    27	
    28	universe u
    29	
    30	open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry
    31	
    32	namespace AlgebraicJacobian.TwoChart.TwistedCoordinates
    33	
    34	variable {I R0 R1 R01 : Type u}
    35	  [CommRing R0] [CommRing R1] [CommRing R01]
    36	
    37	/-- The degree-d base monomials followed by the aligned generators on the
    38	x-chart. -/
    39	def chart0 (d : ℕ) (x : R0) (aa : I → R0) :
    40	    Fin (d + 1) ⊕ I → R0
    41	  | Sum.inl r => x ^ (r : ℕ)
    42	  | Sum.inr i => aa i
    43	
    44	/-- The same degree-d base monomials in reverse order, followed by the
    45	aligned generators on the y-chart. -/
    46	def chart1 (d : ℕ) (y : R1) (bb : I → R1) :
    47	    Fin (d + 1) ⊕ I → R1
    48	  | Sum.inl r => y ^ (d - (r : ℕ))
    49	  | Sum.inr i => bb i
    50	
    51	@[simp]
